question: In Figure 1B-1, what happens immediately after FHWA approves a request to experiment?
model_answer: Direct Answer: According to Figure 1B-1, once the FHWA review results in a "Yes" at the "Approved?" decision point, the immediate next step is that the requesting jurisdiction installs the experimental traffic control device. After installation, the process branches into two parallel activities—evaluating the experimental device and providing semi-annual reports to FHWA Division & HQ—both of which lead to the requesting jurisdiction providing FHWA a copy of the final report. (If the answer is "No," the requesting jurisdiction instead responds to questions raised by FHWA, and the request loops back to FHWA Review.) Standards (mandatory): - Note that experimentation itself requires prior approval: "A traffic control device or application that does not comply with the provisions of this Manual shall not be used on any street, highway, bikeway, or site roadway open to public travel... without first receiving official approval to experiment from the FHWA's Office of Transportation Operations." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 1B-1 shows the "Approved?" diamond with the "Yes" arrow leading directly to the box "Requesting jurisdiction installs experimental traffic control device," which then branches to "Evaluate experimental traffic control device" and "Requesting jurisdiction provides semi-annual reports to FHWA Division & HQ," both flowing into "Requesting jurisdiction provides FHWA a copy of final report." [Image 2] The full page view of Figure 1B-1 confirms the same sequence, including the "No" loop back to FHWA Review via the "Requesting jurisdiction responds to questions raised by FHWA" box. Citations: - Figure 1B-1 (p.7) - Section 1B.05 Support §9 (p.8) - Section 1B.05 Standard §2 (p.6) - Page 48
gold_answer: The requesting jurisdiction installs the experimental traffic control device.
